story.title: United Airlines blocks AI agents from booking flights, citing cybersecurity risks

facts.text: United Airlines will block AI agents from managing customers’ reservations and flight purchases, warning of significant cybersecurity and privacy risks, as well as potential legal violations.
is a reporter covering digital privacy, surveillance technologies and cybersecurity policy for The Record.

“Sharing account credentials with personal, third-party, AI assistants can expose sensitive information, and actions taken by these tools may result in unintended purchases, account changes, or use of MileagePlus miles,” United said in a Wednesday press release .
“Blocking agents or forcing more data sharing just delays the inevitable,” he said via text, arguing for wider use of verified identity tokens.

Automated AI actions also could break Federal Aviation Administration and Department of Transportation rules, the release said, citing the fact that flight check-in requires “human acknowledgment that bags do not contain banned substances like explosives.”
United Airlines is spooked by AI travel agents.
The airline updated its contract to bar AI agents from making, changing, or servicing tickets and from buying seats, upgrades, or other products.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
But each query costs the airline money, and United doesn't want to pay for AI bot queries.
United has the right to cancel such reservations without notice, and the ban reaches AI tools offered through travel agencies.
AI agents can search and display fares, but the traveler must personally complete the booking.
United would still see it as an Expedia booking.
The airline has read the pulse of the people on this one: A fraud-detection survey found 43% of Americans would let AI book with final approval, but only 12% would allow fully autonomous booking.
United Airlines said it will restrict access to AI agents seeking to book flights and manage reservations on their users’ behalf, citing a risk to cybersecurity and undermining federal regulations.
The airline is the latest American corporate giant to prevent customers from using AI agents and autonomous assistants to access their systems.
The airline also warns of a risk of violating federal aviation rules, such as requiring that a human completes flight check-ins to acknowledge that their bags do not contain banned substances.
